verdict.rationale: Lium has built-in termination rules: you set an hours limit, end time, or USD spend cap and the pod is deleted when it is reached (also `--ttl` in the CLI), and per-key budgets are enforced server-side. These are fixed conditions with a single action, not a general user-defined event→action rule system. The availability WebSocket is only an event feed that users must script against themselves, so it earns no credit. Missing for 10: user-definable custom rules/triggers, a choice of actions beyond pod deletion, event-driven automation on events such as GPU availability or job completion, webhooks or outbound callbacks, and independent corroboration.
